title: Rate Difference and Price Protection Claims
summary: Check price-drop, price protection and contract-rate claims against price lists, contracts, stock and sales data, and cap each claim at what the distributor or dealer could really have held.

seo.title: Rate Difference and Price Protection Claims | VipraTech
seo.description: Validate rate difference, price protection and contract-rate claims against price lists, contracts, stock and invoices before credit is issued.

problem.intro: When a brand cuts a price, distributors and dealers claim the difference on stock they already hold. When they sell to hospitals, institutions or key accounts at an agreed rate below list price, they claim the difference back. Both kinds of claim depend on stock and sales data the brand does not fully see.

pain_points.title: Stock in hand that is hard to verify
pain_points.detail: Price drop and price protection claims rely on the claimant's own stock statement on the effective date, which rarely matches what they bought and sold.

pain_points.title: Contract rates scattered across agreements
pain_points.detail: Institutional and key-account rates, validity and eligible customers sit in contracts and emails, not in one register.

pain_points.title: Claims on ineligible sales
pain_points.detail: Sales to customers outside the contract, after it ends or above the agreed quantity are claimed at the contract rate.

pain_points.title: Price lists with many versions
pain_points.detail: Effective dates, regional prices and pack changes make it hard to know which price applied to which invoice.

solution.overview: VipraTech checks each claim against the price list or contract that applied on the date. For price drops and price protection, it estimates the stock the distributor or dealer could have held on the effective date from purchases, sales and earlier stock reports, and caps the claim at that quantity. For contract-rate claims, it checks each sale against the contract's customers, SKUs, rates, validity and quantities, using invoices to those customers. The difference is recalculated line by line, uncertain lines go to an exception queue, and finance approves the credit note sheet.
capabilities: Versioned price lists and contract register, by region, pack and effective date
Stock-on-hand estimate from purchases, sales and earlier stock reports
Checks contract-rate sales against eligible customers, SKUs, validity and quantity
Recalculates the eligible difference for every line
Flags claims above estimated stock or outside the contract
Credit note sheet and audit trail linking claim, price list or contract, and invoice

workflow.title: Receive claims
workflow.detail: Distributors and dealers send price-drop or contract-rate claims with stock statements or invoices to the end customer.

workflow.title: Load prices and contracts
workflow.detail: The price list or contract valid on each date is taken from the register.

workflow.title: Check quantities
workflow.detail: Stock on hand is estimated for price drops; contract sales are checked against eligible customers and quantities.

workflow.title: Recalculate
workflow.detail: The eligible difference is recalculated for every line and compared with the amount claimed.

workflow.title: Exception review
workflow.detail: Lines above estimated stock, outside the contract or without invoices go to finance with the reason.

workflow.title: Approve and credit
workflow.detail: Finance approves the credit note sheet, with the price list or contract linked to every line.

match_rules.rule: Price list version on the date
match_rules.logic: The difference is the old price less the new price in force on the effective date for that region and pack, not the latest list.
Price-drop and protection claims are capped at the stock the claimant could have held: last verified stock plus purchases less sales up to the effective date.
Contract-rate claims count only sales to customers named in the contract, for listed SKUs, within its validity and agreed quantity.
Each contract-rate sale must match the claimant's invoice to that customer, with date, SKU, quantity and billed rate.
The same stock or sale cannot be claimed both as a price drop and at a contract rate, or in two periods.

exception_codes.meaning: The claimed quantity is above the stock the claimant could have held.
exception_codes.action: Approve the estimated quantity and ask for stock records for the rest.

exception_codes.meaning: The claim uses a price that was not in force on the date.
The sale is to a customer or SKU the contract does not cover.
exception_codes.action: Reject, or approve with the contract owner's sign-off.

exception_codes.meaning: The sale falls after the contract ended or past its quantity.
No invoice supports the contract-rate sale.
exception_codes.action: Ask for the invoice to the customer.

human_in_the_loop: Finance approves every credit, and commercial or institutional sales confirm contract terms the register cannot settle. The stock-on-hand estimate is shown with its workings so a person can accept or override it.

Overrides logged with the reviewer and reason
compliance_notes: Price reductions after supply are usually settled by credit note referencing the original invoice for GST; the system keeps that link.

rollout.scope: One recent price change, or the contract-rate claims of one region, with finance-settled claims as the benchmark.

faqs.q: How accurate is the stock-on-hand estimate?
faqs.a: It is only as good as the purchase, sales and stock data available, so it is shown as an estimate with its workings. Finance can accept it, override it or ask for evidence.

faqs.q: Does it cover price protection for electronics and durables dealers?
faqs.a: Yes. Price protection on a price drop is the same check: the dealer's eligible stock on the effective date, multiplied by the drop for each model.

faqs.q: Do you handle government and hospital rate contracts?
faqs.a: Yes. Contracts are entered with their customers, SKUs, rates, quantities and validity, and each claimed sale is checked against them.

faqs.q: Is this the same system as your distributor claims settlement?
faqs.a: Yes. Every VipraTech workflow runs on one claims engine: the document reading, matching, review queue and audit trail are shared. For this workflow we set up your price lists and contracts as versioned rules, along with your document templates and matching keys.
